hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? growing up, what did you and your siblings, or cousins, fight about most?
options: the classic. today, the oldest version of it.
that one stings. today’s story starts there.
then you got all the slices. listen anyway.

steps.line: Now the story comes down to earth, and the first thing it shows is a family. Two sons of Adam each bring an offering to God.
One offering is accepted. The other isn’t. And the brother whose offering was refused says: “I will kill you.”

steps.q: What do you think his brother answers?
steps.why: He points to the heart, not the gift. And then he says something braver still.

steps.line: His brother answers: “God accepts only from the mindful. Even if you raise your hand to kill me, I won’t raise mine to kill you.”

steps.q: He says, “Even if you raise your hand to kill me, I won’t raise mine.” The Qur’an gives his reason. What is it?
o: He was weaker and knew he’d lose
He thought his brother was bluffing
“I fear God, Lord of the worlds”
steps.why: Qur’an 5:28. His restraint isn’t weakness or a gamble. He fears God more than he fears his brother.

steps.line: The Qur’an says simply: his soul talked him into it, and he took his brother’s life. Then God sent a crow, scratching gently at the earth.
Watching it, he learned how to lay his brother in the earth. “Woe is me!” he cried. “Couldn’t I even be like this crow?” And he was full of regret.

steps.q: The Qur’an has a crow show him what to do. What does that say about where he’s fallen?
o: He had to learn decency from a bird
He’d been given a sign of special favour
Crows were the usual guides for the dead
steps.why: The first killer is outdone by a bird, and he knows it: “Couldn’t I even be like this crow?” The Qur’an says he became one of the regretful (5:31).

steps.line: Right after, the Qur’an draws its lesson: whoever wrongly takes one life, it is as if they killed all people. Whoever saves one, as if they saved all.

steps.q: The Qur’an says this rule, one life as all people, was decreed for the Children of Israel. Is there a matching Jewish teaching?
o: Only as a rule about war
steps.why: Qur’an 5:32 begins “for this reason We decreed for the Children of Israel.” The Mishnah (Sanhedrin 4:5) teaches it too: save one life, and you save a whole world.

steps.line: Today, a woman in a first-aid class practices chest compressions on a dummy. One life saved, the Qur’an says, is like saving everyone.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the brother who was wronged said, i won’t raise my hand. and the qur’an turns its saddest story into its biggest promise about life.
in islam, every single life carries the weight of all people. taking one is like taking all. saving one is like saving all.

steps.q: The Qur’an never names the brothers, only “the two sons of Adam.” Why might it tell the story that way?
o: So it could be any family
steps.why: Tradition calls them Qabil and Habil, but the Qur’an doesn’t. Two sons of Adam: that’s every one of us, wherever jealousy starts to whisper.

today.say: today, take one small step toward saving a life: look up a first-aid class near you, learn where the nearest defibrillator is, or check in on someone who’s been quiet lately. one life is like all lives.
options: lovely. that’s the verse, made practical.
beautiful. that can save a life too.

sources: Qur’an 5:27-31 (the two sons of Adam; the offering accepted from one; “I will surely kill thee”; “Allah accepteth only from those who ward off (evil). Even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee to kill thee”; his soul made it seem fair to him; the raven scratching the ground; “Woe unto me! Am I not able to be as this raven?” and he became repentant, Pickthall)
Qur’an 5:32 (whoever kills a soul… it shall be as if he had killed all mankind, and whoso saveth the life of one, it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind)
Qabil and Habil: names from tafsir and tradition (e.g. Ibn Kathir on 5:27), not in the Qur’an
Sahih al-Bukhari 3335 (the first son of Adam bears a share of every unjust killing, as he was the first to establish it)
